entries.effect: -init is defined on UIImageConfiguration as the designated initialiser with no trait collection: a configuration that specifies nothing. The symbols group compares its init and new answers with the host's own
entries.source: the header of SDK 16.4 and the host's own UIKit under Mac Catalyst (macOS 27.0), held against the backport by tests/backports/host/uikit2 (the symbols group); UIKitCore of the arm64e shared cache of iOS 18.0, read with modules/apple/objc.lua's inventory, one pass for the whole set of rows. The controls of that read, because a reader that answered nothing would answer these too: 37248 of the cache's 190858 classes carry `-init` in their own instance list (NSObject among them, and ARConfiguration, whose header marks -init NS_UNAVAILABLE all the same), and a method named `new` is in the own metaclass list of 665 of them, NSObject among them - NSObject declares +new in its own metaclass list rather than leaving it to be inherited. The reader stores every method name with a `-` prefix whichever list it read it from, so the count is of a method NAMED new in that class's own metaclass list, which is the reading these rows rest on; the seven classes here are `no-own-new` in that reading. The header half, measured here with clang -fsyntax-only -fobjc-arc -Wall -Werror=objc-missing-property-synthesis at armv7-apple-ios6.0 and armv7-apple-ios4.3 against the 16.4 SDK: an NS_UNAVAILABLE redeclaration in a class's own @interface draws no -Wincomplete-implementation and an available one does, so an NS_UNAVAILABLE redeclaration forces no definition in the port
